'''Joseph Thomas Hupp''' (born on March 23, 1957) is an American chemist. He is the Morrison Professor of Chemistry in the [[Weinberg College of Arts and Sciences]] at [[Northwestern University]].

==Early life and education==
Hupp was born on March 23, 1957, in [[Cuba, New York]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=PROFESSOR JOSEPH T. HUPP |url=https://chemgroups.northwestern.edu/hupp/josephhupp.html |publisher=Northwestern University |access-date=November 9, 2021}}</ref> He attended Cuba Central School and played on their football team. As a senior, he placed 14th among 114 high school students who took the Nevins Mathematics Contest at [[Alfred University]] and was awarded automatic admission.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hupp wins math honor |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/88618901/hupp-wins-math-honor/ |access-date=November 9, 2021 |publisher=Wellsville Daily Reporter |date=December 16, 1974|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> Despite this, he attended [[Houghton College]] for his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree and [[Michigan State University]] for his PhD.<ref name="bio"/>

==Career==
Following his PhD, Hupp became an associate research assistant at the [[University of North Carolina]] from 1984 to 1986.<ref name="bio"/>  In his final year, Hupp earned the 1986 Presidential Young Investigator Awards and joined the faculty of chemistry at [[Northwestern University]] (NU).<ref>{{cite news |title=Announcements |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/88618535/announcements/ |access-date=November 9, 2021 |publisher=Detroit Free Press |date=March 18, 1986|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> As a professor, Hupp collaborated with five NU researchers to attempt to create artificial enzymes to act as catalysts in chemical reactions.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Swarts |first1=Phillip |title=NU professors get $5 million for enzyme studies |url=https://dailynorthwestern.com/2008/01/23/archive-manual/nu-professors-get-5-million-for-enzyme-studies/ |access-date=November 9, 2021 |publisher=The Daily Northwestern |date=January 23, 2008}}</ref> Following this, he was elected a fellow of [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fellman |first1=Morgan |title=Eight Named AAAS Fellows |url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2012/01/aaas-fellows/ |access-date=November 9, 2021 |date=January 25, 2012}}</ref> and [[Materials Research Society]] for enabling discoveries in the synthesis of porous materials.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chemists Receive Materials Research Society Fellowships |url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2016/03/chemists-receive-materials-research-society-fellowships/ |publisher=Northwestern University |access-date=November 9, 2021 |date=March 29, 2016}}</ref> He also received the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s 2014 Stephanie L. Kwolek Award for "key enabling discoveries in the design and syntheses of functional materials relevant to energy science applications, including light-to-electric energy conversion and supramolecular framework-based sensing, sieving, gas storage and catalysis."<ref>{{cite web |title=RSC Prize Lecture |url=https://www.rsc.org/events/detail/16718/rsc-prize-lecture |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry |access-date=November 9, 2021}}</ref> 

In 2018, Hupp received the George S. Hammond Award from the Inter-American Photochemical Society for "his range of contributions from fundamental work on light-induced electron-transfer reactions to elucidation of mechanisms for molecule-powered solar cells to design and synthesis of new classes of light-harvesting and photocatalytic materials."<ref>{{cite web |title=HUPP RECEIVES 2018 GEORGE S. HAMMOND AWARD FROM I-APS |url=https://chemistry.northwestern.edu/about/news/2018/hupp-receives-2018-george-s.-hammond-award-from-i-aps.html |publisher=Northwestern University |access-date=November 9, 2021 |date=November 20, 2018}}</ref> The following year, he was appointed ''[[Energy & Environmental Science]]''’s Editorial Board Chair<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gempf |first1=Kathryn L. |title=Introducing Energy & Environmental Science's new Editorial Board Chair Joseph Hupp |url=https://blogs.rsc.org/ee/2019/01/03/introducing-energy-environmental-sciences-new-editorial-board-chair-joseph-hupp/?doing_wp_cron=1636457537.0946500301361083984375 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry |access-date=November 9, 2021 |date=January 3, 2019}}</ref> and was listed amongst the 2019 Highly Cited Researchers from [[Clarivate Analytics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FOURTEEN CHEMISTRY PROFESSORS RECOGNIZED AS 2019 HIGHLY CITED RESEARCHERS |url=https://chemistry.northwestern.edu/about/news/2019/fourteen-chemistry-professors-recognized-as-2019-highly-cited-researchers.html |publisher=Northwestern University |access-date=November 9, 2021 |date=November 29, 2019}}</ref> As the Morrison Professor of Chemistry, Hupp was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fellman |first1=Morgan |title=Faculty elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2021/04/faculty-elected-to-american-academy-of-arts-and-sciences |publisher=Northwestern University |access-date=November 9, 2021 |date=April 22, 2021}}</ref>
